title: OLED monitors are finally getting cheaper. I found 5 worth buying

description:
Microsoft is always working to modernize Windows 11’s look. To that end, the company has now replaced old system elements dating back to the Windows 95 era, according to preview leaks.

In a Bluesky post, well-known Windows leaker PhantomOfEarth unveiled a number of new features in the most recent Windows 11 preview builds. Among them is a new File Explorer properties dialog box, for which the underlying code hasn’t changed much over the past few decades.
title: Windows 11 is finally retiring UI relics from the Windows 95 era

description:
There’s nothing quite like the anticipation and excitement of setting up a fresh dorm room ahead of a fresh semester. But a laptop on a wobbly desk won’t cut it for an entire year—you’ll want a proper workstation that’s equipped for maximum comfort and productivity.

We’ve curated a mix of tech and desk gear that’ll level up any college desktop. Whether you’re the student who’s shipping off to school or the parent who’s footing the bill for one, these picks will round out a productive setup that fits real college life.

We’re assuming you already have a laptop, so no laptop recommendations in this list. If you’re in need of one, check out PCWorld’s picks for the best laptops for college students.
title: Heading off to college? The ultimate laptop workstation shopping list

description:
Ask an AI chatbot to brainstorm names for a podcast, Wi-Fi network, or small business. You’ll likely wind up with a list of suggestions that sound a little… well, same-y.

Large language models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini won’t have any problem cranking out a dozen names for your pet project or website. But getting a dozen names that are truly diverse, unique, and punchy? That’s a lot trickier to do—but still possible. You just need to know how to push them the right way in a couple different directions.

title: I asked ChatGPT for 100 ideas. The best ones came later

description:
Most people don’t intentionally publish their personal information online. Yet bits and pieces of it end up there anyway through social media posts, app permissions, shopping habits, and countless websites that quietly collect data behind the scenes. Before long it’s easy for third parties to piece together a surprisingly detailed picture of your life.

The good news is that protecting your privacy doesn’t require throwing away your devices and holing up in a cabin. In many cases, it simply comes down to making small changes to how you use the apps and services you rely on every day. If your information is already out there, privacy-focused data removal services can also help reduce your exposure by requesting that data brokers remove your personal records. 

Here are seven ways you might be making your personal information public online—a
title: Stop! 7 ways you’re making your personal info public online

description:
Windows 11 is chock full of options, many just cosmetic. But there are some settings which can significantly affect your PC’s productivity performance, so much that I specifically pay attention to them each time I boot up a brand new PC.

If not properly managed, some settings can literally slow down your PC. Others, if adjusted correctly, can actually speed it up by a moderate amount.

Case in point: the Windows performance option. Remember the “turbo button” on the first PCs? When released, the PC was set to a compatibility mode that slowed the PC down to about 4MHz. When pushed in and activated, the PC ran at its rated speed — 33MHz or 66MHz, generally — giving you the performance you paid for.

Welcome to PCWorld’s Smart Mode newsletter! The focus is productivity: f
title: 3 Windows settings that can make or break your PC

description:
